Affront

/ə-FRONT/ — stress on second syllable, rhymes with font · verb

Hear It

What It Means

To affront someone is to insult them or offend their dignity, usually through disrespectful words or behavior.

Serving the guest of honor last was taken as a deliberate affront.

Worked Example

A diplomat was seated below junior staff members at an official state dinner — a calculated slight intended to diminish her nation's standing.

Affront captures both the deliberate nature and the targeting of someone's dignity or honor. It is more precise than 'insult' (which could be accidental) or 'embarrassment' (which lacks the intentionality aimed at status).

How Affront Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

insult

insult: to say something deliberately hurtful

snub

snub: to ignore or reject someone coldly

disrespect

disrespect: to treat someone as unworthy of courtesy

Antonyms

honor

honor: to show public respect for someone

compliment

compliment: to praise someone sincerely and kindly

How Strong Is It? — rudeness → insult → snub → affront

rudeness vs. affront

rudeness vs. affront: Rudeness is far weaker than an affront: rudeness is general bad manners, while an affront is a pointed act of disrespect aimed straight at someone's dignity.

insult vs. affront

insult vs. affront: An insult is weaker than an affront; an insult is hurtful words, but an affront is an open, often public act that offends someone's honor to their face.

snub vs. affront

snub vs. affront: A snub is weaker than an affront: a snub coldly ignores someone, while an affront openly and deliberately attacks their dignity.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — af-

Prefix — af-: to, toward (form of ad-) (Latin)

Root — front (frons, frontem)

Root — front (frons, frontem): forehead, face (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: An affront is literally an insult delivered 'to the face' — Old French afronter even meant 'to slap in the face.' The word keeps that idea of open disrespect: an affront offends someone's dignity right in front of them, out in the open.

Use the root in a new word: confront

Use the root in a new word: confront: She turned to confront her accuser face to face — the same Latin root front, 'forehead, face,' that makes an affront an insult thrown at someone's face.

Root Check

Word Choice

formal / literary

Affront is a formal word for calculated, intentional insult aimed at someone's honor or standing. Use it when the disrespect is clearly deliberate and touches on status or dignity. For everyday rudeness, 'insult' is simpler and sufficient.
